title: The Right to be Forgotten in Federated Learning: An Efficient Realization with Rapid Retraining
sum_llm_few-shot: In machine learning, the right to be forgotten led to the concept of machine unlearning, enabling data holders to erase their data from models. Traditional methods require full access to training data. Federated Learning offers an alternative but challenges exist. This paper addresses these issues by proposing a rapid retraining approach for machine unlearning in federated settings. The solution preserves model utility efficiently while allowing local control over training data.

title: Sequential Recommendation via Stochastic Self-Attention
sum_llm_few-shot: Sequential recommendation models predict the next item based on past behavior, but handle uncertain user actions poorly. STOSA, an STochastic Self-Attention, addresses this by embedding items as distributions and incorporating uncertainty. It uses Wasserstein Self-Attention to learn item-item relationships and a new regularization term to ensure positive vs. negative item dissimilarity.

title: A Generative Neural Annealer for Black-Box Combinatorial Optimization
sum_llm_few-shot: We introduce a generative, end-to-end solver for black-box combinatorial optimization that combines sample efficiency and solution quality. The model treats the black-box objective as an energy function and trains a neural network to approximate the Boltzmann distribution, capturing different levels of exploration based on temperature. This allows it to learn the energy landscape and optimize efficiently even when queries are costly.

title: SA-CAISR: Stage-Adaptive and Conflict-Aware Incremental Sequential Recommendation
sum_llm_few-shot: SA-CAISR is a Stage-Adaptive and Conflict-Aware Incremental Sequential Recommendation framework designed for real-world applications requiring frequent updates. It addresses high costs associated with replay-based and regularization-based methods by operating solely on the old model and new data, using a novel Fisher-weighted knowledge-screening mechanism to identify and remove outdated knowledge while retaining compatible patterns. The method achieves state-of-the-art performance in incremental SR, improving Recall@20 by 2.0% and reducing memory usage by 97.5%, as well as training time by 46.9%.

title: Measuring Re-identification Risk
sum_llm_few-shot: A new theoretical framework measures re-identification risk in compact user representations, formalizing the probability of obtaining identities from these representations. The framework applies to Chrome's Topics API, demonstrating its utility through both theory and practical attacks.

title: Memory-Guided Multi-View Multi-Domain Fake News Detection
sum_llm_few-shot: The proposed M FEND framework addresses challenges in multi-domain fake news detection through a multi-view approach, utilizing a Domain Memory Bank to enhance domain-specific knowledge and a Domain Adapter to integrate diverse view data effectively. Experimental results on English and Chinese datasets confirm the framework's efficacy.

title: A Constraint Propagation Approach to Probabilistic Reasoning
sum_llm_few-shot: The paper shows how strictly following probability theory can coexist with concurrent, self-activated constraint propagation for managing uncertainty, allowing simultaneous activation of predictive and diagnostic inferences while propagating beliefs harmoniously toward stability.

title: Modelling Stopping Criteria for Search Results using Poisson Processes
sum_llm_few-shot: A new method predicts document relevance in text retrieval systems, allowing users to set a minimum recall and probability threshold. Evaluated against existing methods, it outperforms them.

title: Optimal Cost Almost-sure Reachability in POMDPs
sum_llm_few-shot: This paper explores partially observable Markov decision processes with integer costs, showing that approximating the optimal cost is undecidable but presenting algorithms for both exact and approximate solutions when costs are positive.

title: A Framework for History-Aware Hyperparameter Optimisation in Reinforcement Learning
sum_llm_few-shot: A reinforcement learning system's performance can be enhanced through an integrated framework combining complex event processing and temporal models, which allows efficient and non-intrusive exploration of hyperparameters during real-time operation. The framework dynamically adjusts hyperparameters based on historical data, leading to better optimization of hyperparameters and improved training stability and rewards.
